body:
Part of splitting task:3254586664024306. From its notes 1, 2 and 8–12; the original notes stay on the parent record. These all concern `extract::rust` moving tests and helpers.

- **Needless borrows (note 1).** `extract::rust.test_groups` and `extract::rust::visibility.promote_access` pass `&ids` where `ids` is already a `&HashMap`, making it `&&HashMap` (`belongs_in_test_file(ix, &ids, i)`, `can_promote(ix, &ids, …)`). `rewrite_move` also passes `&ix` where `ix` is already `&Index`. Pass `ids` and `ix` directly. Check: `cargo clippy` in `solace-cli` reports no `needless_borrow` in these functions, and `rust-unit` stays green.
- **Hidden static promotion (note 2).** `extract::rust.promote_hidden_static` can promote a line inside a multi-line or raw string in a `thread_local!` block that starts with `static NAME:` instead of the declaration. Find the declaration by its `syn` span, or have `language::rust_refs.thread_local_names` return positions, because only the parsed declaration is reliable. Check: a unit test with a raw-string line `static SECOND: x` above the real declaration, asserting that only the real declaration gains `pub(crate)`.
- **`use super::*` (note 8).** `extract::rust.needs_super` was changed from `moved[used] || module == target` to `!moved[used] && module == target`. The target test file now gets no `use super::*` for moved references; they are rewritten to full paths instead. Four older tests had their `use super::*` assertions removed to match. Restore `use super::*` and leave references to moved items in the target's parent unqualified, so test bodies stay byte-identical and nothing is reported unused. Check: in `a_partial_test_move_leaves_staying_tests`, assert that `helpers_tests.rs` contains `use super::*;` and `assert_eq!(make(), 1);`, and that `check --warnings` is clean.
- **Inline container imports (note 9).** `extract::rust.carry_test_imports` follows the `use super::*` chain only when there is no inline container (`container.is_none()`). An inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; ... }` in the crate root that uses `testing::Scratch` still loses that import when it moves, because `super` sites are skipped. Apply `carry_super_glob` to `test_container_imports` sites as well. Check: a test with an inline `mod tests` in `lib.rs` that uses `testing::Scratch`; one extract writes `use crate::testing;` and type-checks.
- **Ancestor imports (note 10).** `carry_super_glob` and `super_glob_module` carry only module names. A moved test that uses a name the ancestor imports (for example a root `use std::collections::HashMap;`, seen through `use super::*`) still breaks. `test_covered` skips `use` uses, so the test moves anyway. Carry ancestor `use` sites that the moved tests mention too. Check: root `lib.rs` has `use std::collections::HashMap;` and a file-backed test uses `HashMap`; after the extract, `check` is clean.
- **Glob-reach module (note 11).** `extract::rust.super_glob_module`, `sees_through_super_glob`, `has_super_glob` and `is_super_glob` repeat the same glob-chain loop in the already large `extract::rust`. Move them into `extract::rust::glob_reach`, built on one chain iterator that both use. Then `parent_module` does not need to become `pub(crate)`. Check: `extract::rust` gets smaller, the walk is written once, and the three new tests still pass.
- **Repeated scan (note 12).** `extract::rust.staying_tests_reply` reruns `test_covered` for every test function in the crate and then does a linear `find` over all symbols. Reuse the `outside`/`locals` sets that `move_tests` already computes, or iterate `outside ∪ locals` directly instead of `0..ix.syms.len()`. Check: the reply in `a_file_backed_test_that_reaches_staying_code_stays_and_is_named` is unchanged.
title: extract: test moves carry imports
